scope: Federer 3.2.27, pp. 262–263, with a necessary local correction to its upper bound. The actual finite coordinate projection masses satisfy the square-root sum-of-squares lower bound and coordinate-sum upper bound on every Hausdorff-measurable finite (H^m,m)-rectifiable W in R^n, m<=n, in all natural degrees. The lower bound keeps arbitrary-source scope whenever the displayed actual integrals exist; their nonnegativity and finiteness are derived. A genuinely one-rectifiable nonmeasurable two-sheet set with finite outer length has actual coordinate masses one and zero but outer length greater than one, disproving the printed unrestricted upper bound.
proof_route: Specify the actual coordinate counting integral laws independently. State absolute orthonormal-coordinate replacement laws and prove a local witness by finite basis synthesis, norm preservation by Parseval and contraction by coordinate absolute value. Finite source mass proves L1 membership; existing opaque vector integration and continuous dual evaluation give actual finite masses and both bounds. Identify coordinate projection norms through the actual injection, exterior adjoint and one-dimensional target top power. Extend actual projection multiplicity integrability to completed measurable sources using a Borel sandwich and exact fibres outside its null projected excess. Apply the actual 3.2.20 area formula and 3.2.25 orientation. For the arbitrary-source lower bound and finiteness, use true rectifiable Borel measure hulls and actual fibre monotonicity without assuming hull differences null. Prove the local upper-bound counterexample using 2.2.4 on the unit interval, complementary subsets on two parallel segments, closed-segment measure splitting, strict finite regular-measure split excess, actual univalent horizontal fibres and vertical counts supported on two null target points.

The preceding p. 262 line 14 correction to 3.2.20 is retained in the area-formula adapters.
